core.title: Keep each function's cyclomatic complexity at or below 10
core.given: Any production source function (3+ code lines, outside test files and the stack-wide excluded trees), whether changed or not
core.when: its cyclomatic complexity (1 + each decision point counted by the stack's complexity measure) exceeds 10
core.then: Restructure it to score at or below 10 by separating decisions into coherent, nameable responsibilities without changing behaviour.
prefer: Diagnose first: group branches by policy/responsibility, separate validation and guards from the core operation, spot repeated compound conditions that are a domain predicate.
Extract a coherent decision or policy into an intention-revealing function.
Replace repeated compound conditions with well-named predicates.
Dispatch table/strategy only for a genuinely stable key-to-behaviour mapping.
Keep the caller's control flow showing the important choices.
avoid: Moving the same branch tree unchanged into a generically named helper.
Indirect data structures or opaque encodings used solely to lower the score.
Scattering one policy across tiny functions whose interaction is harder to follow.
Changing boolean semantics, branch order or fallback behaviour.
unless: Function with fewer than 3 code lines (not scored: a two-line function is not a complexity problem).
Test file or any tree on the stack-wide exclusion list, e.g. vendored or build output (outside the scan).
core.why: Complexity approximates the test cases needed to pin behaviour; above ~10 paths full coverage stops being written and defects settle in untested paths. The score senses too many decisions in one responsibility; hiding branching only hides the signal.
evidence: The stack's metrics check reports no complexity finding for the triggering function (the triggering violation is gone).
Existing behaviour and path-focused tests remain green.
Extracted code introduces no new nesting, duplication or length violation, and the refactor introduces no new violations of the stack's conventions.
Reviewer confirms the resulting decision boundaries correspond to meaningful responsibilities that are easier to name, test and reason about, rather than a relocated or opaquely encoded branch tree.
verification: Threshold: cyclomatic complexity <= 10 per function; a score above 10 is a finding. Applies to every in-scope function, changed or unchanged (no baseline).

Counting: complexity = 1 + each decision point; a decision point is a construct adding an independent path. Which constructs count is given by the stack's complexity measure (its control-flow branch forms, short-circuit and nullish operators, and conditional expressions).
Trivial function: a function under three code lines is skipped and not scored.

Scan scope: production source only. Test files and the stack-wide excluded trees (vendored and generated code) are outside the scan; the exact exclusion list is the one stack-wide list, not owned by this rule.

The threshold and the counting arithmetic belong to this rule's shared definition and must not drift between stack realizations: a repository that switches realizations must see the same numbers - only the tool that runs the count differs.
Disposition strict: the check fails on every finding; no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline (existing violations in unchanged code are findings too). Severity 3.

Realized by the stack's metrics detector (a validator): it scores every in-scope function, changed or not, and emits this rule's finding for each function above the threshold; where such a detector already exists, only its output needs consuming - no new observer.

fires: An existing, unchanged production source function of 3+ code lines already scores 11 or more - strict scope has no baseline, so it fires too.
A new or edited production source function of 3+ code lines scores 11 or more (1 + the decision points the stack's measure counts).
A refactor adds branches or boolean operators to a function, pushing it above 10.
doesNotFire: A function with fewer than 3 code lines, however many operators it has.
Functions in test files or in the stack's excluded (vendored/generated) trees.

profileRequirements.bunValue: complexity = 1 + each decision point. Decision points: if / else if / for / while / do / catch / case keywords, each && / || / ?? operator, each ternary.

profileRequirements.meaning: The one stack-wide list of vendored and generated trees that are never scanned; this rule's 'outside vendored/build dirs' exclusion is that list.

neutralityNotes: The rule is substantively stack-neutral: threshold 10, the '1 + each decision point' formula, the 3-code-line trivial-function minimum and the strict disposition are kept in the core because the rule itself demands they not drift between realizations; only the concrete decision-point construct list is stack-specific and is supplied through the proposed key idiom.source_syntax#complexity_measure. Generalizations made: 'TypeScript/TSX source function' -> production source function (profile: tooling.languages, suffix.source); 'test, vendored and build dirs' -> test files plus the one stack-wide exclusion list (roots.excluded), with the checker's ownership of the exact list kept in verification; 'a two-line arrow' -> 'a two-line function'; 'no new ATDD Bun violations' -> 'no new violations of the stack's conventions'; the fires/doesNotFire examples speak of production source functions instead of .ts/.tsx files. Detector, finding and alias ids (bun_ts_metrics_detector, COMPLEXITY-CYCLOMATIC-TS-001) and the python-pytest sibling transcription note remain bunOnly.
